jobs.descriptionHtml:
The role

As an AI platform engineer, you'll build the products, interfaces, and tools that accelerate frontier research for Applied Compute’s customers. You'll own the full stack of our application platform including the system that powers collaborative human-AI workspaces, the backend workflows that orchestrate sandboxed agent sessions, and the SDK that gives engineers control and visibility over the entire agent development lifecycle. You'll work closely with product research engineers to integrate new platform capabilities like memory, context, and auto-research into polished user experiences, and with applied research engineers to build for customer deployments and upstream learnings back into the platform.

What You'll Do

  • Own the full stack of our platform, AC2

  • Integrate new platform capabilities like memory, context, and auto-research

  • Design new interfaces for interacting with agents, including the platform console, dashboards, resource management views, and observability UIs

  • Build tools that allow subject matter experts to capture and communicate their workflows

  • Develop the AC SDK that internal and customer-facing engineers use to build domain-specific agents and applications

  • Build the agent sandboxing UX and deployment surfaces that let agents operate across different environments

What We're Looking For

  • Strong full-stack engineering skills with experience shipping production web applications

  • Deep familiarity with LLM-powered applications and agent architectures

  • Extremely creative and open to prototyping: you love putting together a demo and showing people what's possible

  • You care deeply about what the user actually experiences and think carefully about who the user is before you build

  • Experience with both real-time and asynchronous systems

  • Ability to build and iterate on polished, functional applications quickly with high engineering craft

Strong Candidates Also Have

  • Previous experience as a founder or early engineer at a zero-to-one company

jobs.title: Research Scientist
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The Role

As a research scientist, you will design, implement, and optimize our frontier reinforcement learning stack as well as the recipes that we run on it. This work sits where algorithms and systems meet—we believe that the best results come from people who can move between them seamlessly. Algorithmic ideas only matter if they run reliably at scale. Systems only matter if they make models learn better and faster. Working closely with other researchers, you’ll close that loop: algorithmic advances get tested at scale, systems work gets judged by what it does for learning, and what you learn goes straight into the recipes and infrastructure our customers rely on.

 

What you’ll do

  • Design, run, and analyze RL experiments, scoping them carefully to separate real algorithmic gains from noise

  • Develop and improve post-training algorithms, reasoning about why they work (or don’t) and diagnosing failures like instability, reward hacking, and collapsing exploration

  • Design and optimize our RL training and inference pipelines across large GPU clusters

  • Understand how systems choices affect learning (low-precision numerics, off-policy staleness, distributed training edge cases, etc.)

  • Partner with applied researchers to bring frontier post-training capabilities into production deployments

What we’re looking for

  • A strong foundation in probability, statistics, machine learning, and reinforcement learning, including policy gradient methods, variance reduction, and the tradeoffs between on-policy and off-policy training

  • The ability to learn quickly and navigate ambiguous or underspecified problem settings

  • Fearlessness and curiosity to understand things, with an eye for details in specific algorithms or the training stack

  • Experience programming with and managing training jobs on large-scale GPU systems

  • A bias toward fast implementation, paired with a high bar for rigor, reliability, and efficiency

  • Familiarity with open-weights models (architecture and inference)

  • Background in reinforcement learning or integration of inference with RL training loops

Strong candidates also have

  • Published research or substantial projects in RL, post-training, or LLM reasoning and alignment

  • Demonstrated technical creativity through published projects, OSS contributions, or side projects

  • Experience with distributed training frameworks (PyTorch, JAX, DeepSpeed)

  • Background in high-performance computing or working with large-scale clusters

  • Contributions to open-source ML infrastructure

The role

As an applied research engineer, you’ll own customer engagements end-to-end: understanding their data, their workflows, and their problems, then building and deploying agents that deliver real value. jobs.title: Platform Research Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The role

As a platform research engineer, you'll do research around ways to make Applied Compute's platform intelligent. This includes how we set up continual learning against production traces (OPSD, SDPO, RMSD), scaling synthetic environments, data & evaluations, and integrating the RL stack that powers agent improvement over time. Your research will serve as the connective tissue between our AI product engineers (who build the interfaces and tools customers use) and our applied research engineers (who work directly with customers to ship agents into production). Your job is to take learnings from across customer deployments, identify the greatest common denominators, and pursue research to accelerate all of our deliveries.

What you'll do

  • Build and improve our hinting primitives for online self-distillation: the algorithms and systems that allow agents to learn continuously from production traces and company data

  • Develop and maintain trace search, trace mining, and data labeling systems that feed the continual learning loop

  • Research and implement approaches to multi-agent system design, including structuring agent coordination and managing trade-offs

  • Build best in class coding agents for automatically creating agents for delivery and hill-climbing harnesses

  • Translate learnings from applied research and customer deployments into generalizable platform features

  • Collaborate closely with AI product engineers to ensure new ML capabilities are integrated into polished platform experiences

What we're looking for

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals combined with deep ML/AI knowledge

  • Production research experience: both deliveries train models into production & top-tier conference publications, blogs, or reports

  • Strong experimental design skills: you are diligent, don't cut corners, and actually run experiments

  • Highly organized: you manage complexity across multiple workstreams

  • Ability to read and translate research papers and prototypes into shippable engineering

Strong candidates also have

  • Experience with reinforcement learning

  • Background in building evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, or data quality systems

  • Experience with continual learning/distillation

  • Opinions about multi-agent system architectures and the trade-offs between different approaches

  • Published work or open-source contributions in AI/ML systems

jobs.descriptionHtml:
The role

As the founding strategic account executive, you'll win new business and drive revenue for Applied Compute across the F500. You'll help enterprises understand what Specific Intelligence looks like inside their organization. You'll leverage your consultative sales expertise to become a trusted partner to customers, helping them embed and deploy AI and scale into a multi-workstream partnership over time.   • Win new business and drive revenue for Applied Compute. Find the right entry points at prospective customers, educate them on what Specific Intelligence is and why it's different, and guide them from first conversation through close. You'll own the full sales cycle end-to-end

  • Maintain client partnerships over time to grow engagements into multi-workflow partnerships

  • Sell into senior technical buyers (CTOs, Heads of AI/ML, VP Engineering) with confidence and credibility

  • Spearhead market expansion by identifying new customer segments, industries, and use cases. Collaborate cross-functionally with applied research, product, and leadership to refine our positioning and sustain a competitive edge

jobs.title: Platform Security Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The role

As the platform security engineer, you'll help shape Applied Compute's security posture as we scale. We train custom models on the most sensitive thing our F500 customers have — their proprietary workflows, institutional knowledge, and production data — and we deploy autonomous agents back into those environments. Our customers rely on us being uncompromising about how we handle their data, credentials, and execution boundaries. We've built strong foundations to earn that trust and we're investing heavily in the people and systems to take it to the next level.

This role demands a security practitioner who thinks like an attacker, builds like an engineer, and has the judgment to know where to invest. You'll partner closely with infrastructure, product, and applied research engineers to make security a first-class concern from design through deployment. You'll also help us pioneer what AI-native defense looks like — using our own agent stack to detect, investigate, and pre-empt threats at machine speed. We're building security to defend against the strongest attackers with access to the most capable LLMs.

What you'll do

  • Shape the security architecture of our platform end-to-end, from data and credential handling to agent execution and customer deployments

  • Lead threat modeling and secure design reviews; identify and prioritize the risks, attack surfaces, and assumptions that matter most

  • Drive our offensive security program: continuously stress-test our platform, agents, and pipelines against the kinds of adversaries we should actually expect to face

  • Build the tooling, automation, and detections that scale security across the company — including agent-based systems that turn our AI capabilities into a defensive force multiplier

  • Partner with engineers across the company to instill secure-by-default practices and remove classes of risk through better design

  • Own the security guarantees we present to enterprise customers and their CISOs

  • Lead incident response when it matters: detection, containment, communication, and durable fixes

  • Build our security teams as we grow

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in platform security and cyber defense

  • Have an exceptional eye for finding flaws others miss, and instinctively ask "how would I break this"

  • Lead with a strong grasp of offensive security, anticipating risk from an adversary's perspective rather than checking compliance boxes

  • Bring a builder's mindset — you have experience shipping secure software to production

  • Have strong judgment to identify the most important security vulnerabilities and put into practice

  • Reduce risk through secure design and simplicity; advocate for fundamentals like least privilege, defense-in-depth, and minimizing complexity

  • Are energized by ambiguity and high autonomy

Strong candidates also have

  • Hands-on experience securing complex cloud and multi-tenant environments, especially ones deployed inside customer VPCs

  • Familiarity with AI/agent-specific risks: prompt injection, tool use abuse, data and model exfiltration

  • Background in offensive security, vulnerability research, or red teaming against cloud or AI systems

  • Experience using LLMs to accelerate security workflows — detection, investigation, triage, or automated response

  • Track record taking compliance programs (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP) to completion as engineering efforts

jobs.descriptionHtml:
The role

At Applied Compute, compute is our core input that makes our post-training and agent infrastructure possible. As Compute Analyst, you'll run the analyses behind how we source, price, and use the GPU capacity that powers everything we train, serve, and deploy for our customers. You'll work closely with the finance and research teams to turn a fragmented, fast-moving supply market into clear numbers the company can make big decisions on. This role suits someone who wants to learn the economics of AI infrastructure from the inside, with real ownership from day one.

 

What you'll do

  • Build and own the models behind our compute unit economics, including effective $/GPU-hour, cost per training run, cost per token served, utilization, and goodput

  • Track the global GPU market: pricing, availability, and terms across hyperscalers, neoclouds, regional operators, and emerging providers, plus outline the tradeoffs between hardware generations

  • Support live negotiations with quote benchmarking, scenario analysis, side-by-side comparisons of term sheets and contract structures, and deal memos that make the recommendation clear

  • Work with research and engineering to turn training roadmaps, RL workloads, and inference growth into concrete capacity forecasts

  • Monitor our fleet: commitments, reservation coverage, idle capacity, and utilization by workload, helping surface problems before they become costly

  • Partner with finance on compute budgeting, commitment tracking, and margin analysis across our training and inference products

  • Build TCO models that combine pricing, reliability, acceptance-testing results, and goodput data to inform sourcing decisions

  • Automate the reporting and dashboards that give leadership a real-time view of our compute position

What we're looking for

  • 2–5 years in a highly analytical role, such as investment banking, private equity, consulting, strategic finance or FP&A, or cloud/infrastructure analytics

  • Excellent financial modeling skills and native fluency in unit economics, margin structure, and scenario analysis

  • Strong technical skills: comfortable in SQL and Python, and happy to pull and clean your own data

  • Real curiosity about the AI compute market: providers, accelerators, pricing dynamics, and where things are heading

  • Clear communication, with the ability to explain complex analysis simply to finance, engineering, and leadership

  • High ownership, with a habit of seeing gaps and building the fix before anyone asks

jobs.title: Strategic Partnerships Lead - Ecosystem & Channel
jobs.descriptionHtml:
As the Strategic Partnerships Lead - Ecosystem & Channel at Applied Compute, you’ll build the partnerships that don’t yet have a playbook. This is a hands-on role dedicated to partnerships. You’ll spend your time sourcing, structuring, negotiating, and operating partnerships with open-source model labs, human data companies, research groups, and the systems integrators and consulting firms that carry our work into enterprises.

Much of this ground is greenfield: you’ll define what a partnership with Applied Compute looks like for each kind of counterparty, prove it with a first deal, and turn it into a program. You’ll own each partnership from first conversation through signed agreement and ongoing results, with responsibility for its structure, economics, and business impact.

You’ll work closely with our sales, research, product, and leadership teams to decide which partners matter, bring them in, and turn each relationship into pipeline, capability, and revenue as the company grows.

What you’ll do

  • Build model and data partnerships. Source, structure, and close partnerships with open-source model labs, human data companies, and other research and data counterparties. Negotiate the licensing, co-development, distribution, and data-supply arrangements that give Applied Compute and our customers the models, data, and access we need.

  • Build the channel. Stand up and run our partner program for systems integrators and consulting firms. Recruit the right firms, enable their teams via our platform and services, and build the referral, resale, and delivery structures that let partners bring us into their enterprise accounts.

  • Open new partnership categories. Identify counterparties we haven’t worked with before, from evaluation and benchmark providers to domain-expert networks and industry consortia. Define what a partnership with Applied Compute looks like for each, and close the first deal that proves the model.

  • Turn partnerships into pipeline. Run the co-selling, co-marketing, and account-mapping motions that convert partner relationships into qualified opportunities for our sales team, and work those opportunities alongside our account executives.

  • Own the partner operating system. Build the agreements, enablement materials, and tracking that make partnerships repeatable as the ecosystem grows. Manage ongoing relationships with executive sponsors and day-to-day counterparts at each partner.

  • Measure and improve results. Instrument partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, revenue, and capability. Use those results to decide where to invest more, where to pull back, and which new partnerships to pursue.

What we’re looking for

  • Prior professional experience in strategic partnerships, alliances, or business development at an AI lab, data company, infrastructure company, or enterprise software company, with a track record of closed partnerships that produced measurable revenue.

  • Experience structuring and negotiating complex commercial agreements, including licensing, co-development, data-supply, resale, and referral arrangements.

  • Existing relationships with partner and business development teams at open-source model labs, human data companies, or large systems integrators.

  • Enough technical depth to hold your own in conversations about model training, post-training data, and inference, and to work directly with researchers and engineers on joint projects.

  • Strong commercial judgment: you can tell which partnerships will move the business, say no to the rest, and structure deals that work for both sides.

  • Comfort with ambiguity: you can build a partnership category from nothing, with no template to follow and no precedent to point to.

jobs.title: Developer Relations Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the role
As a Developer Relations Engineer your focus will be technical content, demos, and distribution. Your work will help developers and researchers discover AC2, understand what they can build, and put it to work.

You’ll work directly with researchers and engineers, run experiments yourself, and turn the results into useful technical resources. You’ll define our DevRel strategy and standards, with the opportunity to hire and lead a team as the function grows.

What you will do

  • Build runnable demos and cookbooks. Show developers how to train a decision model, evaluate a router, or deploy a trained checkpoint. Include code, sample data, expected results, and explanations that make each example reproducible.

  • Explain our technical work. Partner with researchers to publish technical articles, walkthrough videos, and interactive demos. Explain the methods, results, tradeoffs, and limitations so developers can judge where an approach is useful.

  • Own distribution. Get technical work in front of relevant developers through X, GitHub, developer communities, and collaborations. Experiment with topics and formats, and use the response to improve what we create and where we share it.

  • Educate developers. Run workshops, livestreams, and office hours. Speak at relevant events, and build a tutorial series spanning evaluation, training, and deployment.

  • Help developers succeed with AC2. Help new organizations get set up, run their first evaluation and training job, and interpret the results. Turn questions and recurring problems into resources other developers can use.

  • Improve the developer experience. Improve quickstarts and troubleshooting guides. Bring specific, reproducible problems to engineering and help prioritize improvements.


What you bring

  • A strong engineering background. You can independently build, test, and debug useful demos and example applications.

  • Hands-on experience fine-tuning and evaluating language models. You can explain your training setup, evaluation design, and what you learned from the results.

  • A track record of clear technical writing. You have published articles, tutorials, documentation, or other work that helps developers understand and apply technical concepts.

  • Experience getting technical work in front of developers, and an interest in experimenting with new ways to reach and teach them.

  • You listen closely, welcome technical feedback, acknowledge uncertainty, and enjoy helping developers work through problems.

  • The judgment and initiative to define priorities, take projects from idea to publication, and build a function that can grow beyond your own work.

Strong candidates also have

  • An established audience among AI developers, particularly on X / Twitter.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
THE ROLE


As a Research Product Manager, you will drive model training engagements with customers. You will understand the customer’s data, objectives, and success criteria, and work with researchers to build and execute on model training plans. This role requires a broad skillset: on any given day, you’ll flex across product, research, engineering, and GTM functions.

What You'll Do

  • Drive the roadmap for research engagements. You’ll work with customers to translate their needs into research requirements. You’ll work with researchers and engineers to execute on model training engagements.

  • Own relationships with customers. You are the primary interface between the customer and our research and engineering teams. You’ll make sure that the customer’s needs are understood and that we are driving impact for their business.

  • Deeply understand model behaviors. You’ll spend time staring at traces, building taxonomies, hunting for pathologies, and critiquing evals.

  • Bring research learnings into the product. You’ll drive the productization of research techniques from customer engagements into the AC2 training platform.

What We're Looking For

  • Clear communication. In this role, you will interface with researchers, technical buyers, engineers, and salespeople. Your job is to drive clarity amongst them. You should excel at explaining complex topics in simple terms.

  • Technical rigor. You are someone that researchers and engineers trust to lead a model training engagement. We expect you to understand the capabilities of the systems we build, and you should have programming experience. You should have hands-on experience building with LLMs and strong familiarity with coding agents.

  • Strong commercial sense. You’ve worked with enterprise customers and have strong customer empathy.

  • High slope. You’re a fast learner. You don’t need to have experience in model pre- or post-training, but you should be able to ramp quickly on any technical topic.

Strong Candidates Also Have

  • Experience working at an enterprise AI company

  • Educational background in computer science or mathematics

  • Experience at companies with forward-deployed or customer-facing engineering cultures

  • Experience working in management consulting, with technical experience before or after

  • Familiarity with model pre-training or post-training techniques, including reinforcement learning
